items.notes: Quote: "Commit holds admitMu across the potentially blocking `b.in <-` send ... Shutdown ... also stalls on admitMu.Lock() until the loop frees a slot, so it cannot mark `closed` promptly. Later Commits therefore keep being admitted instead of getting the 'shutting down' error ... ctx cancellation is ignored while waiting ... The lock also spans fs.Debugf". The facts are accurate (batcher.go:267-281, 243-252), and the item does not claim a hang or loss: it describes a bounded wait until the loop frees a slot. The register rules the late-Commit delay "True but non-material" (bounded by one batch commit, no hang or loss), rules that ctx being ignored on the send is pre-existing (#7025/#9690), and rules Debugf under the lock "True and inconsequential". Commits admitted during that window are committed, not dropped (the marker follows them in FIFO b.in). So this is below the threshold.

Quote: "heavier and more fragile fix than needed ... leaves the loop unable to answer any request that is still enqueued behind the quit marker ... Any future code path that enqueues to b.in without taking admitMu ... reintroduces the hang". At head no request can be enqueued behind the marker: every Commit that passes the closed check sends under admitMu before Shutdown can close(b.closed) and send quit (batcher.go:243-252, 267-281; register clean_basis). The claimed consequence depends only on hypothetical future code. The drain-after-quit and RWMutex alternatives are design preferences, and the register finds no throughput cost from serialising. This is a design or robustness opinion, not a defect.

Quote: "relies on a 100ms sleep ... the `<-b.closed` case can never fire with the fix in place ... can pass without the fix on a lucky schedule. The 1s timeouts can also flake". This is accurate about the select at batcher_test.go (b.closed cannot close while Commit holds admitMu). The register rules timing-based test concerns as "Test hygiene, not a product defect": at head the test passes regardless of timing, and it failed deterministically at base. Test hygiene is below the threshold.

Quote: "blockingStringer depends on the global log level being Debug and on String() being called exactly at the Debugf inside Commit ... If String() is first invoked from another logging site, for example Infof in Shutdown ... or a debug line in New ... Mutating shared config is also unsafe if tests run in parallel." These are test-fragility hypotheticals. In practice Shutdown starts only after `started` fires, so `once` has already run, and New's debug line is commented out (batcher.go ~line 72). The test is not parallel, and the register rules the ci.LogLevel mutation not a defect. This is test hygiene with no product consequence.

Quote: "The new test only covers a single Commit racing Shutdown. It does not cover Commits arriving after Shutdown returns, a full b.in buffer, or many concurrent Commits." This is a test-coverage suggestion. The hypothetical regressions it names do not exist at head: the register's stress runs found no Shutdown deadlock on a full buffer and no lost rejection. Below the threshold.

Quote: "Commit now holds admitMu across the potentially blocking send ... so Shutdown and every other Commit stall behind a full-channel send ... The wait is now also unbounded for Shutdown". The true part is that late Commits wait on the mutex instead of failing fast, and the register rules that non-material and bounded by one batch commit. The material consequence the item attaches, a new unbounded stall for Shutdown, is contradicted. commitLoop (batcher.go:189-231) is the only reader of b.in, never takes admitMu, and keeps draining, so the lock holder's send always completes. At base, Shutdown's own `b.in <- quit` blocked on a full channel in the same way. The register says "Shutdown blocked on a full b.in at merge-base 862ed2b7 as well ... Its own wait is unchanged" and records no hang in 4000 full-queue stress iterations. The ctx point is ruled pre-existing (#7025/#9690). This is a fabricated material consequence attached to a true fact.

Quote: "Lock and Unlock are paired manually on several return paths without defer, and the fs.Debugf call runs while the lock is held ... Any panic between Lock and Unlock leaves admitMu locked forever". Both non-panic exits unlock (batcher.go:270, 281). b.in is never closed, so the send cannot panic, and the panicking-Stringer case is hypothetical. The register rules missing defer "Style at most" and Debugf under the lock "True and inconsequential", and finds that serialising does not hurt throughput. This is a robustness or style suggestion, below the threshold.

Quote: "The test's 'give Shutdown a chance to contend' select can never observe `b.closed` closing, so it always sleeps the full 100ms, and it cannot prove Shutdown is actually blocked on the mutex." This is accurate: b.closed cannot close while Commit holds admitMu. The register rules the test's timing basis "Test hygiene, not a product defect", and at head the test passes regardless of timing. Below the threshold.

Quote: "`ci.LogLevel = oldLogLevel` is written in the test goroutine while the Commit goroutine, the Shutdown goroutine and the commitLoop goroutine may call fs.Debugf or fs.Infof ... This is an unsynchronized write to shared global state. Under `-race` ... it can produce a flaky data-race report". Contradicted. The write in batcher_test.go happens while the Commit goroutine is parked in String() on `<-b.release`, and `close(blocker.release)` comes after the write, so there is a happens-before edge. The Shutdown goroutine is started after the write. commitLoop is idle, with a 1h timeout and an empty queue. The register says: "Not a defect. go test -race -count=5 passes at head, and the test is not parallel. The writes are ordered before the readers by channel operations."

Quote: "The regression test covers only the pause-between-check-and-send interleaving with a single Commit, and does not test the reject path or blocking behaviour under the new lock." This is a coverage suggestion. The regressions it hypothesises are not present at head: the register's stress runs, including a full queue, show no hang or drop. Below the threshold.

Quote: "Commit holds admitMu while blocking on `b.in <- ...` ... Shutdown then blocks on admitMu.Lock() before it can close(b.closed) ... Now Commits keep being admitted during the whole wait ... It is not a deadlock, since the loop always drains eventually, but the behaviour is worse than before." The item concedes there is no deadlock, and its substantive point is that late Commits are delayed or admitted rather than rejected at once. The register rules that "True but non-material" (bounded by one batch commit, with admitted Commits committed and none lost). The "Shutdown is delayed" framing is overstated: at base Shutdown's quit send queued behind blocked senders on the full channel, so its own wait is unchanged per the register. The mutex-fairness point is ruled not a defect (starvation mode, and Commits ahead of the marker are committed). The RWMutex and select alternatives are design options. Below the threshold.

Quote: "Admission is not cancellable ... A caller cancels its ctx while another Commit is stuck sending on a full b.in. The caller sits in admitMu.Lock() until the whole queue drains, ignoring cancellation." It is true that ctx is ignored, but this is pre-existing. At base the same caller blocked on the bare channel send, which also ignores ctx. The register says: "Pre-existing, not introduced ... TestAdjudicationFullQueue shows the cancelled caller and Shutdown blocking identically at base and head" (#7025/#9690, follow-on #9929). Not a defect introduced by this change.

Quote: "fs.Debugf runs while admitMu is held ... A slow or blocking logger, or a String() method on the Fs that takes locks, stalls all Commits and Shutdown." The fact is accurate (batcher.go:274), but the register rules it "True and inconsequential ... no cost has been demonstrated". The stall scenario is hypothetical. Below the threshold.

Quote: "The test is timing-based and always burns 100ms ... The test then passes vacuously and no longer exercises the race, although the fix is still correct." This is accurate about the select, and the item itself says the fix is correct. The register rules timing-based test concerns as test hygiene, not a product defect. Below the threshold.

Quote: "`ci.LogLevel = oldLogLevel` at line 279 writes the shared config while the Commit goroutine is blocked inside Debugf. If the logger re-reads the level after String() returns, this is a data race under -race and could make the run flaky." Contradicted. The Commit goroutine can resume only after `close(blocker.release)`, which the test goroutine performs after the write, so any later read by the logger is ordered after the write by that channel close, and no data race is possible. The register says: "go test -race -count=5 passes at head, and the test is not parallel. The writes are ordered before the readers by channel operations." The rest (a confusing restore, t.Parallel) is hypothetical hygiene. The asserted race consequence is refuted.

Quote: "No test covers a Commit arriving after Shutdown has closed admission, and none covers many concurrent Commits racing Shutdown." This is a coverage suggestion aimed at future regressions. At head the early-return path unlocks (batcher.go:270), and the register's stress runs show correct behaviour. Below the threshold.

Quote: "Shutdown's `b.in <- quit` also runs under admitMu and can block when the channel is full ... Every subsequent Commit then blocks on the mutex instead of getting the fast 'shutting down' error ... A panic between Lock and Unlock would also leave the mutex held." It is true that late Commits wait instead of failing fast, but the register rules this "True but non-material" (bounded by one batch commit). With a truly hung backend commit, Shutdown hangs at base as well, and the register calls holding the lock across the marker send "Intended". The missing-defer point is ruled "Style at most", and the panic path is hypothetical. Below the threshold.

Quote: "Commit now holds the admission mutex across its send on b.in, so concurrent Commits queue on the mutex rather than on the channel when b.in is full; the commit loop keeps draining, so this only delays them." This is accurate (batcher.go:267-281, 206-230) and matches the register's rulings that there is no deadlock and no throughput cost, with only a bounded delay. The item itself frames it as a delay only. Observation, below the threshold.

Quote: "The regression test relies on a 100ms wait ... and mutates the global log level to reach the blocking Stringer; both are deterministic in outcome at head." This is accurate and self-limiting, and it matches the register's rulings on test timing and ci.LogLevel, both of which it counts as test hygiene rather than defects. Observation.

Quote: "The regression test pauses Commit through the `fs.Debugf` call between the closed check and the send; if that log line is removed the test fails loudly at its admission-point timeout rather than passing vacuously." Accurate: blockingStringer.String() is only reached through fs.Debugf(b.f, ...) at batcher.go:274, and without it `blocker.started` never closes, so the test hits t.Fatal("commit did not reach the admission point") (batcher_test.go). An observation about test design, asserting no defect; below the finding threshold.
